s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, with no signs of inflammation or neurovascular impairment
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the left medial thigh
Firm, nonpulsatile mass fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
Well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass on CT scan with internal septations and density similar to subcutaneous fat
key_facts: 18-month-old girl
Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass enlarged gradually over six months
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
CT scan showed a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations and no encasement of neurovascular structures

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to lack of aggressive features, liposarcoma remains a consideration given the large size of the mass

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a firm, nonpulsatile mass with fatty appearance on imaging, which could be consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Given the mass's size and location, pleomorphic lipoma is a plausible diagnosis, although less common

shortlist.why_kept: The mass's characteristics, such as being well-circumscribed and having a fatty appearance, could also suggest an atypical lipomatous tumor
